elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The insertion reads "no more than once per year", which on a literal reading permits a calendar-year (or contract-year) measure rather than a rolling "any 12-month period" window, allowing two inspections in close succession across a year boundary. To reach the preferred wording the drafter would need "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company".
Retained: "during the Company's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection is performed by "HDI's General Manager"; no independent auditor requirement was inserted.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered contains no confidentiality undertaking applicable to the inspecting person; nothing was added.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site/copy-delivery language appears in the rendered clause; the right is simply to "inspect the records" at the Company during business hours.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional Vendor cost-bearing, which is at least as favourable as the 5% cost-shift carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the granted right is limited to inspecting "the records ... reasonably related to the calculation of such payments", and the finding records that no other audit/verification or system-access right exists in the Agreement, so no system-access language needed deleting.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted by operation 1: "may, no more than once per year and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice"; deterministic check "audit frequency limited" ok.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Existing "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day floor.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Existing "fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" is unconditional and therefore better than the 10% carve-out.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted frequency cap supplies the only missing fallback element, while the retained 30-day notice and unconditional HDI-borne cost language already satisfy the other two.

Preferred level is not reached: no independent-auditor requirement (the inspector remains "HDI's General Manager"), no confidentiality undertaking for the auditor, no off-site-where-possible language, and "once per year" is not the rolling "any 12-month period" anchor.

Minimality holds: the edit is a five-word insertion into the existing sentence; favourable existing terms (30 days' notice, business hours, records-only scope, HDI cost-bearing) are untouched and no extras (survival, expense, procedure or damages language) were added.

Intent preserved: the sentence remains grammatical ("may, no more than once per year and upon ... notice, have the right to inspect"), the cross-reference to "such payments" and the second sentence on fees are unaffected, and no defined term or reference is left dangling.
Severity remains medium: the gap was an uncapped frequency in an otherwise notice-limited, cost-shifted, records-only inspection right, not remote system access or unannounced audits.
